title: The Lyra Technique II: SVD Denoising and Directional Projection
subtitle: Two new measurement channels extend KV-cache geometry to emotion and persona detection
abstract: Corrected November 2026: the emotion result this paper built on decodes the emotion a generator was asked to write into a third-person story, from cache keys, not through W_K and not the user's state; its 30-class accuracy (12.3x chance) does not beat a text (TF-IDF) baseline, its binary AUROC 0.992 (n = 300) is confounded with arousal, and the injection test is withdrawn; the source paper is under correction. SVD denoising appears to reveal hidden signal, raising persona intensity from AUROC 0.611-0.751 to 0.899-0.992; however, the denoising deltas fall within the max-over-rank selection envelope (0/16 exceed it), so the raw AUROCs are the defensible numbers and the denoised values are reported as upper bounds pending nested CV. Dominant singular values carry scale; residual values carry discriminative structure. Denoising is a calibration tool, not a universal amplifier.
